# lucidity_scaling_policy_attachment (Resource)

Attaches a lucidity_scaling_policy to one instance. Destroying it detaches the policy. One policy can be attached to many instances: use one attachment per instance. Every refresh checks which policy the instance actually has; if it has none or a different one (changed outside Terraform), the next apply attaches this policy again.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One attachment per instance; a policy can be attached to many instances.
resource "lucidity_scaling_policy_attachment" "orders_db" {
  policy_id = lucidity_scaling_policy.db.id

  instance_identifier = {
    cloud_provider            = "AWS"
    cloud_provider_account_id = "123456789012"
    instance_id               = "i-0abc123def4567890"
  }
}

# Azure needs the resource group; instance_id is the VM name.
resource "lucidity_scaling_policy_attachment" "azure_vm" {
  policy_id = lucidity_scaling_policy.db.id

  instance_identifier = {
    cloud_provider            = "AZURE"
    cloud_provider_account_id = "8f2d1c3a-5b6e-4f70-9a81-2c3d4e5f6a7b"
    resource_group            = "prod-rg"
    instance_id               = "vm-db-01"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_identifier` (Attributes) The instance to attach the policy to. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--instance_identifier))
- `policy_id` (String) ID of the scaling policy to attach (lucidity_scaling_policy.<name>.id).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) "<policy_id>/<cloud_provider>/<cloud_provider_account_id>/<instance_id>" (with "/<resource_group>" before the instance ID for Azure). Also the import ID.

<a id="nestedatt--instance_identifier"></a>
### Nested Schema for `instance_identifier`

Required:

- `cloud_provider` (String) AWS, AZURE, or GCP.
- `cloud_provider_account_id` (String) The AWS account ID (12 digits), Azure subscription ID, or GCP project ID.
- `instance_id` (String) The instance ID (the VM name in Azure).

Optional:

- `resource_group` (String) AZURE only, and required there: the VM's resource group.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# "<policy_id>/<cloud_provider>/<cloud_provider_account_id>/<instance_id>"
terraform import lucidity_scaling_policy_attachment.orders_db 33/AWS/123456789012/i-0abc123def4567890

# Azure: "<policy_id>/AZURE/<subscription_id>/<resource_group>/<vm_name>"
terraform import lucidity_scaling_policy_attachment.azure_vm 33/AZURE/8f2d1c3a-5b6e-4f70-9a81-2c3d4e5f6a7b/prod-rg/vm-db-01
```
